business_problem: NTPF managed a large and growing patient waiting-list workload through a time-consuming Excel-based process that made it hard to assign patients, share accurate data across hospitals, and report performance in real time.
solution_summary: NTPF and Spanish Point built the Patient Access Management System on Microsoft Power Platform to replace a manual, Excel-based waiting-list process with governed case management. Patient waiting-list data is pulled from a SQL database into Dataverse, where Power Apps present role-specific views for NTPF staff and hospitals to assign patients, update case status, and manage inpatient and outpatient workflows. Azure DevOps provides visibility across development, test, and production, while Power BI dashboards publish operational and public reporting. Responses and scanned correspondence are written back to Dataverse, giving NTPF a central system of record that can scale with annual funding increases, enforce security through Microsoft configuration rather than custom code, and drive real-time performance management.

solution_components.name: Power Platform
solution_components.role: Provides the low-code foundation for the Patient Access Management System and its security model.

solution_components.name: Power Apps
solution_components.role: Delivers model-driven applications for NTPF staff, hospital users, and call-center workflows.

solution_components.name: Dataverse
solution_components.role: Stores patient case data, scanned responses, and workflow state for the central case-management system.

solution_components.name: Azure DevOps
solution_components.role: Controls development, test, and production promotion for Power Platform applications.

solution_components.name: Power BI
solution_components.role: Publishes dashboards and reporting on patient metrics and operational performance.

data_flow: Patient waiting-list data is pulled from a SQL database into Dataverse, processed in Power Apps by NTPF and hospital users, updated as patients move toward treatment, and then surfaced through Power BI dashboards and external reporting.
business_outcome: NTPF scaled PAMS from a 30,000-patient starting point to more than 160,000 managed patients, reduced waiting times, and gave staff and hospitals faster, more secure access to actionable case data.
metrics: Patients managed through PAMS grew from 30,000 to over 160,000
Over 30,000 Offers of Care were issued in the first five months
45% of those Offers of Care were accepted
Model-driven apps were designed at one tenth the cost of a UX designer
architecture_clues: Role-based views in Power Apps for NTPF and hospital users
Dataverse is the central store for case data and scanned responses
Azure and Power Platform security was configured rather than custom-built
evidence_quotes: Patient waiting list data is pulled from a SQL database into Dataverse and NTPF employees use a Power Apps application to search and select patients from the list.

PAMS quickly delivered beyond expectations. Just 5 months after its launch, over 30,000 ‘Offers of Care’ had been issued to 41 public hospitals in Ireland via PAMS, 45% of which have since been accepted.
PAMS is fundamental to everything we do at NTPF – and Power Platform is a key part of our system’s success.
